set.reason: The geometric point-and-distance interpretation motivates polar form. Algebraically, r=sqrt(a^2+b^2), cos(t)=a/r and sin(t)=b/r give the representation and quadrant through trigonometric signs without a separate complex-plane interpretation. Preserve preparation rather than requiring the whole geometric interpretation.
set.scope: polar radius and argument interpretation in the complex plane

set.reason: Polar form gives arguments 2*pi*k/n and regular-polygon placement. Cyclic and geometric-sum identities, and low-degree factorization such as z^3-1, work without de Moivre.
set.scope: polar construction of equally spaced roots
